run_label: Experimental print and radical visual culture: Picabia 391, WSPU, La Vie Parisienne
purpose: Build a coherent mini-collection of three original Dada 391 issues and related early 20th century feminist and risqué visual print culture, using existing archive folders and preserving rights evidence.

items.name: Outsider-Art/Francis-Picabia-391-Dada-Issue-01-1917.pdf
items.creator: Francis Picabia
items.license: Public domain (Picabia died 1953; US publication pre-1931; Wikimedia Commons PD)
items.description: Complete four-page inaugural issue of 391, Picabia's anarchic experimental Dada magazine; foundational primary-source avant-garde print ephemera.

items.name: Outsider-Art/Francis-Picabia-391-Dada-Issue-08-1919.pdf
items.creator: Francis Picabia
items.license: Public domain (Picabia died 1953; US publication pre-1931; Wikimedia Commons PD)
items.description: Complete eight-page 1919 Dada 391 issue; a deliberately anti-establishment experimental periodical.

items.name: Outsider-Art/Francis-Picabia-391-Dada-Issue-19-1924.pdf
items.creator: Francis Picabia
items.license: Public domain (Picabia died 1953; US publication pre-1931; Wikimedia Commons PD)
items.description: Final issue 19 of Picabia's 391 magazine, providing a long-range comparison with the 1917 and 1919 issues.

items.name: Feminism/Alfred-Pearse-Votes-for-Women-WSPU-1910.jpg
items.creator: Alfred Pearse, for Women's Social and Political Union
items.description: Original Edwardian British women's suffrage graphic; visual ephemera complementing feminist books and essays.

items.name: Erotic-Art/Charles-Martin-La-Vie-Parisienne-May-1914.jpg
items.creator: Charles Martin
items.license: CC0 1.0 per Wikimedia Commons file page
items.description: Les extravagances de demain, illustrated 1914 La Vie Parisienne magazine artwork, capturing prewar Parisian risqué visual culture.
